page.text:
With ordered pairs established, we can define the *Cartesian product*
$A \times B$, named in honor of René Descartes. The Cartesian product
gathers all ordered pairs $(a, b)$ such that $a \in A$ and $b \in B$:
$$A \times B := \{(a, b) : a \in A \land b \in B\}$$ The Cartesian
product is the foundational arena of modern mathematics: binary relations
on $A$ are defined as subsets of $A \times A$, and functions from $A$ to
$B$ are defined as special subsets of $A \times B$.
